payload.fact: Rockwell interviewed technicians with 20 to 30 years of experience, structured their knowledge by symptom, cause, and response, combined it with records, and put a text-and-voice interface beside the machine; it reports average repair time fell from 18 to 12 minutes.
payload.expected: Putting maintenance knowledge behind a chatbot would mainly be a model-and-manuals project.
payload.actual: The result depended on extracting unwritten experience, structuring it for retrieval, and delivering it beside the failed machine.
payload.tension: The apparently simple chatbot required substantial knowledge-capture and interface work.
payload.target: The shortcut of treating knowledge retrieval as a chatbot installation.
payload.reader_realization: The model was the visible layer; making decades of experience retrievable was the work.

angles.line: Putting 30 years of shop-floor knowledge in a chatbot sounds simple until the interviews, structure, and point-of-use interface show up.
The conversational interface could answer at the machine only after Rockwell did the unglamorous work of capturing what veteran technicians knew.
The maintenance knowledge looked like a document-search problem until Rockwell interviewed the people carrying the unwritten part.
Knowledge in a corpus still was not job knowledge until the technician could reach it beside the broken machine.
Calling the result a chatbot gives the visible interface credit for the interviews and information design underneath it.
